recommendations.title: Note When Symptoms Happen
recommendations.description: Keep a short diary of symptoms, where you were and what you were doing. It helps your doctor link this result to real-life reactions.

recommendations.title: Discuss Results With an Allergist
recommendations.description: Share this report with an allergist or your doctor, especially if you have regular symptoms. They can decide whether more tests are useful.

recommendations.title: Know Emergency Warning Signs
recommendations.description: If you ever have trouble breathing, throat or face swelling, fainting or widespread hives after exposure, call emergency services at once.

recommendations.title: Keep Animals Out of the Bedroom
recommendations.description: If you share your home with an animal, keep it out of the bedroom so you sleep in a space with less hair and dander.

recommendations.title: Clean Animal Hair and Bedding Often
recommendations.description: Wipe surfaces with a damp cloth, vacuum regularly and wash animal bedding often to remove hair, dander and dried droppings.

recommendations.title: Wash Hands After Handling Animals
recommendations.description: Wash your hands with soap after touching animals, bedding or feathers, and avoid touching your eyes or face before washing.

recommendations.title: Get Advice Before Rehoming a Pet
recommendations.description: A positive blood test alone does not prove a pet is causing symptoms. Speak to an allergist before making any decision about a loved pet.

recommendations.title: Protect Yourself Around Farm Animals
recommendations.description: When cleaning sheds or handling cattle, goats, sheep or pigs, use gloves and a well-fitted mask and work in a ventilated area.

recommendations.title: Clean Cages and Lofts Carefully
recommendations.description: Clean bird cages, coops and lofts in open air when possible. Damp-wipe surfaces instead of sweeping, and wear a mask while cleaning.

recommendations.title: See a Doctor for Lasting Cough Near Birds
recommendations.description: If you have a cough or breathlessness that keeps returning after time with birds, ask a doctor to check your lungs.
recommendations.review_note: Bird-related lung conditions are not IgE-mediated; wording kept non-diagnostic. Needs a cited source.

recommendations.title: Limit Contact With Mice and Their Droppings
recommendations.description: In homes or labs, keep mice and bedding contained, use gloves, and clean with a damp cloth rather than dry sweeping.

recommendations.title: Wash Bedding Regularly
recommendations.description: Wash sheets and pillow covers every week in hot water, following the fabric label, and dry them fully in sunlight or a dryer.
recommendations.review_note: Cochrane review (eczema) found only very low quality evidence for avoidance measures; keep wording practical and non-promissory.

recommendations.title: Use Dust-Proof Mattress and Pillow Covers
recommendations.description: Zipped covers made for dust mites can limit contact with mites living in mattresses and pillows. Wipe them clean every few weeks.

recommendations.title: Keep Rooms Dry and Airy
recommendations.description: Mites like humid rooms. Open windows when outdoor air is dry, use fans or a dehumidifier if available, and dry clothes outdoors.

recommendations.title: Dust With a Damp Cloth
recommendations.description: Wipe shelves, fans and furniture with a slightly damp cloth, as dry dusting can lift dust into the air.

recommendations.title: Cut Down Dust-Collecting Items
recommendations.description: Limit heavy curtains, thick carpets and many soft toys in the bedroom, and wash or air out the ones you keep.

recommendations.title: Wear a Mask While Cleaning
recommendations.description: Wearing a mask while sweeping, dusting or clearing store rooms may reduce sneezing and coughing from stirred-up dust.

recommendations.title: Store Dry Foods Properly
recommendations.description: Keep grains, flour and cereals in clean, sealed containers and protect them from dampness.

recommendations.title: Keep Storage Areas Dry
recommendations.description: Store sacks and containers off damp floors and away from leaking walls, and let kitchen cupboards air out regularly.

recommendations.title: Reduce Dust in Store Rooms
recommendations.description: Clean cupboards and store rooms regularly, and avoid shaking out old flour, grain sacks or spilled cereals indoors.

recommendations.title: Check Flour and Grains Before Use
recommendations.description: Throw away flour, grains or cereals that look clumpy, smell musty or show tiny moving specks. Buy smaller quantities when possible.

recommendations.title: Take Care Around Hay and Straw
recommendations.description: Handle hay, straw and animal feed outdoors where you can, keep them dry, and wear a mask when moving or shaking them.

recommendations.title: Dust Books and Shelves Gently
recommendations.description: Wipe books and shelves with a damp cloth, keep storage areas dry, and wear a mask when handling very old or musty paper.

recommendations.title: Check Local Pollen and Air Quality
recommendations.description: On days when outdoor pollen or dust is likely to be high, plan outdoor activity for times when you notice fewer symptoms.

recommendations.title: Rinse Off After Time Outdoors
recommendations.description: Wash your face and hair and change clothes after long periods outside to remove pollen you may carry indoors.

recommendations.title: Limit Pollen Indoors in Your Peak Season
recommendations.description: On days when symptoms are worse, keep windows closed during high-pollen hours and dry clothes indoors or in a dryer.

recommendations.title: Take Care With Cut Grass and Lawns
recommendations.description: Avoid mowing or playing on freshly cut grass during your symptom season, or wear a mask and glasses if you must.

recommendations.title: Tell Your Doctor About Itchy Mouth With Raw Produce
recommendations.description: If raw fruit or vegetables make your mouth or throat itch, tell your doctor. Pollen allergy can sometimes be linked to such reactions.

recommendations.title: Fix Leaks and Damp Walls
recommendations.description: Repair leaking pipes, roofs and damp walls promptly, as moulds grow where surfaces stay wet.

recommendations.title: Ventilate Kitchen and Bathrooms
recommendations.description: Use exhaust fans or open windows while cooking and bathing, and wipe away water from windows and tiles.

recommendations.title: Clean Small Mould Patches Safely
recommendations.description: Clean small patches with detergent and water, wearing gloves and a mask. For large areas, ask a professional to help.

recommendations.title: Avoid Damp Leaf Piles and Mouldy Storage
recommendations.description: Stay away from compost heaps, rotting leaves, damp basements and mouldy stored items, especially if they worsen your symptoms.

recommendations.title: Ask Your Doctor What This Result Means
recommendations.description: Candida normally lives on skin and in the gut. This result alone does not show infection or allergy, so ask your doctor to interpret it.
recommendations.review_note: Needs a cited source for the clinical relevance of Candida-specific IgE.

recommendations.title: Reduce the Chance of Stings
recommendations.description: Wear shoes outdoors, keep food and drinks covered outside, and stay calm and move away slowly if a bee or wasp is near.

recommendations.title: Leave Nests to Professionals
recommendations.description: Do not try to remove hives or nests yourself. Ask trained pest or bee-removal services to deal with them.

recommendations.title: See an Allergist After a Strong Sting Reaction
recommendations.description: If a sting ever caused hives away from the sting, swelling of the face or breathing trouble, ask an allergist for a proper review.

recommendations.title: Store Food in Sealed Containers
recommendations.description: Keep food, pet food and rubbish covered or sealed so cockroaches have less to eat, and take out waste daily.

recommendations.title: Control Cockroaches at the Source
recommendations.description: Seal cracks, fix leaks and use pest control methods as needed. Clean kitchens, drains and under appliances regularly.

recommendations.title: Prevent Mosquito Bites
recommendations.description: Use nets, screens and repellents suitable for your age, and remove standing water around the home where mosquitoes breed.

recommendations.title: Keep Food and Waste Covered
recommendations.description: Cover cooked food, keep bins closed and use window screens to reduce houseflies in kitchens and eating areas.

recommendations.title: Reduce Moths Indoors
recommendations.description: Use window screens and avoid leaving bright lights on near open windows at night, as moths are drawn to light.

recommendations.title: Keep Eating Foods You Tolerate
recommendations.description: Do not stop a food you eat without problems just because of this result. Ask your doctor before removing foods from your diet.

recommendations.title: Think Back to Past Reactions
recommendations.description: Ask yourself whether this food ever caused symptoms soon after eating. Share your answer with your doctor, as history matters more than this result alone.

recommendations.title: Ask About a Supervised Food Challenge
recommendations.description: If the picture is unclear, an allergist may suggest eating the food under medical supervision. Never try this at home.

recommendations.title: Do Not Test Foods at Home After a Serious Reaction
recommendations.description: If this food ever caused a serious reaction, avoid eating it again until an allergist has assessed you in a medical setting.

recommendations.title: Ask Which Related Foods Need Care
recommendations.description: Some foods share similar proteins. Ask your doctor whether any related foods need caution, rather than avoiding them on your own.

recommendations.title: Read Food Labels if Allergy Is Confirmed
recommendations.description: If a doctor confirms an allergy to this food, check ingredient labels and ask about ingredients when eating out.

recommendations.title: Report Reactions That Start Hours Later
recommendations.description: If symptoms after red meat start several hours after eating, tell your doctor. Some meat allergies cause delayed reactions linked to tick bites.

recommendations.title: Ask About the Dust Mite Link
recommendations.description: Shellfish and dust mites share a similar protein, so a positive shellfish result may sometimes reflect mite sensitization. Your doctor can help sort this out.

recommendations.title: Mention Pollen Allergy When Reviewing Spices
recommendations.description: Some spice reactions are linked to pollen allergy, such as mugwort. Tell your doctor if you have hay fever or itching after spices.

recommendations.title: Link Symptoms to Specific Drinks and Treats
recommendations.description: Note whether symptoms really follow coffee, tea or chocolate. Many reactions to these have other causes, so discuss them with your doctor.

recommendations.title: Do Not Change Your Medicines on Your Own
recommendations.description: Do not stop, restart or try any medicine again based on this report. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist first.

recommendations.title: Ask for a Proper Drug Allergy Assessment
recommendations.description: Only a specialist can judge whether a medicine caused a past reaction. Ask your doctor about referral to an allergist.

recommendations.title: Keep a Record of Medicine Reactions
recommendations.description: Write down the medicine, date, dose, symptoms and how soon they started. This record helps your doctor far more than a blood test alone.

recommendations.title: Tell Your Healthcare Providers
recommendations.description: Tell your doctors, dentist and pharmacist about any medicine reaction you remember, so they can choose treatments carefully.

recommendations.title: Ask About Proper Penicillin Allergy Testing
recommendations.description: If you think you are allergic to penicillin or similar antibiotics, ask an allergist about proper testing instead of relying on this blood test.

recommendations.title: Ask Which Pain Relievers Are Safe
recommendations.description: Reactions to pain relievers can have different causes. Ask your doctor which alternatives are safe for you before using any.
recommendations.review_note: NSAID/paracetamol cross-reactivity statements require a cited source before expansion.

recommendations.title: Ask About Skin Patch Testing
recommendations.description: Rashes after numbing creams or sprays are often checked with skin patch tests by a dermatologist or allergist.

recommendations.title: Mention All Ingredients to Your Doctor
recommendations.description: If you reacted to a vitamin product, tell your doctor the exact product. Other ingredients can also be responsible.

recommendations.title: Look at Where Symptoms Happen
recommendations.description: Notice whether symptoms improve on holidays or weekends away from work or hobby materials. Share this pattern with your doctor.

recommendations.title: Speak to an Occupational Health Doctor
recommendations.description: If symptoms seem linked to your job, an occupational health doctor can assess exposure and suggest safe ways to work.

recommendations.title: Choose Latex-Free Products
recommendations.description: If latex bothers you, ask for non-latex gloves and products at work and when visiting clinics or dentists.

recommendations.title: Tell Your Doctor About Fruit Reactions
recommendations.description: Some people with latex reactions also react to fruits such as banana, kiwi or papaya. Tell your doctor if this happens to you.

recommendations.title: Ask About Patch Testing for Henna Reactions
recommendations.description: If henna products cause skin redness, itching or swelling, ask a dermatologist whether patch testing is appropriate.

recommendations.title: Reduce Fibre Dust and Skin Contact
recommendations.description: Use good ventilation, gloves and washing after handling rough fibres or dusty materials, and avoid shaking them out indoors.

recommendations.title: Ask Your Doctor What This Result Means
recommendations.description: This result can reflect past or present exposure to the parasite, or similar proteins. Your doctor will decide whether further checks are needed.

recommendations.title: Wash Hands and Produce Well
recommendations.description: Wash hands before eating and after using the toilet, gardening or handling pets, and wash fruit and vegetables well.

recommendations.title: Follow Your Vet's Deworming Advice
recommendations.description: Regular deworming of pets as advised by a vet, and washing hands after handling soil or pets, helps limit worm exposure.

recommendations.title: Handle and Cook Fish Carefully
recommendations.description: Buy fish from trusted sellers and cook it well. Cooking lowers infection risk but may not remove allergen proteins, so discuss symptoms with a doctor.

recommendations.title: Read Total IgE With Your Doctor
recommendations.description: Total IgE alone cannot explain symptoms. Share your report with your doctor, who can read it with your history and the specific IgE results.
recommendations.review_note: Statement that total IgE alone cannot confirm or exclude allergy is tied to E01 (diagnosis rests on history plus specific IgE or skin test). Reviewer to confirm.
